quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: You are driving in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move into the left lane. You should:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you before changing lanes.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Check your side mirror for traffic and turn on your signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: If you need to slow down while driving on a slippery road, the first thing you should do is:

options.text: Press your brakes hard.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Use your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: On a slippery road, take your foot off the gas pedal first. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with steady, light pressure.

questions.question: The best way to deal with a driver tailgating you is to:

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you and them.
Slam on your brakes to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors every few seconds to watch for tailgaters. If another car is following too closely, slow down gradually to let it pass. Most rear-end collisions happen because a driver is following too closely.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign:

options.text: Warns of existing or possible hazards.
Alerts drivers to school zones.
Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.
Alerts drivers to upcoming food and gas locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns of existing or possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards on or near the road. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: You are driving when it begins to rain. You should:

options.text: Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When rain reduces visibility, slow down. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see clearly, drive to the shoulder and stop until the rain lessens.

questions.question: To prepare for anything coming up on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Look at the entire road and both sides constantly.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and both sides constantly.
questions.explanation: Look ahead and scan the entire road, including both sides. This helps you spot problems early. Do not stare at just the center of the road.

questions.question: You may honk your horn when you:

options.text: Have to stop quickly.
Are passing another car.
Have lost control of your car.
Are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers of the danger.

questions.question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Get out of the car and look for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get the attention of other drivers.
Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You will be found more easily in your vehicle. Walking in a snowstorm is unsafe.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle:

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because it is unlikely another vehicle is coming.
By driving on the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on a hill or in a curve because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never pass by driving on the shoulder. Never cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross because a train is unlikely to be coming.
Dangerous.
Safe places to park a car.
A place where you must always stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains coming from either direction. Follow all signs, signals, and instructions from flaggers. Only cross when you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Slow down, move to create a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to create a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, you must slow down, create a clear path, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Use your four-way flashers.
Use your parking lights.
Not use any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: You must turn on your headlights at dusk and on overcast days. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, when should you signal?

options.text: Just before you change lanes.
At any time.
After you change lanes.
Early enough so other drivers know your plan.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know your plan.
questions.explanation: Signal early before you pass so other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should NOT:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers your plan. Check for other drivers who may also be moving into the same lane.

questions.question: What can help drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.
Accelerating quickly.
Slowing down gradually.
Braking suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Every sudden stop uses fuel to speed back up. Drivers who look ahead can slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid hard braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Always drives slowly.
Watches what other drivers do.
Drives at the same speed all the time.
Only drives in areas they know well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Even experienced drivers can get distracted. A defensive driver watches for what other drivers are doing and prepares for possible problems.

questions.question: When you are in a travel lane on the road:

options.text: You can stop to drop off passengers.
You can stop to look up an address.
You can make a U-turn or back up if you miss a freeway entrance.
Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep driving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your exit, do not back up. Go to the next exit or find a safe place to turn around.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle coming from the right.
The vehicle coming from the left.
The vehicle whose driver honks first.
The vehicle traveling faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control signs or signals, you must let the vehicle coming from the right go first.

questions.question: Driving at night requires more caution because:

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There are more vehicles on the road at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: At night it is dark and drivers cannot see as well as during the day. From 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or when people or vehicles are not visible from 500 feet away, you must use your headlights.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and look for pedestrians and cross traffic.
Slow down without stopping.
Come to a complete stop and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and look for pedestrians and cross traffic.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely and check for pedestrians and traffic. Wait until the intersection is clear before driving on.
